:
This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent No.1 and 2 under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- with interest.

2. The petition averments briefly stated as under; That on 01.01.2023 at about 12.30 p.m. petitioner was traveling in a Car bearing Reg. No.KA-41-P-5894 SCCH-5 along with his colleagues on Bengaluru - Mysuru Road, near Basava Gayhathri Ashrama, Kumbalagodu, Kengeri Hobli,
Bengaluru, which was being driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner with excessive speed and lost control over the vehicle and dashed against the centre divider and then dashed against centre flyover pillar, as a result of this car was moved reverse and dashed against left side grill wall.
Due to the said impact, petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Rajarajeshwari Medical College Hospital, after first aid he was shifted to Basavanagudi Medical Centre and took treatment as inpatient.
3. At the time of the accident, petitioner was aged about 30 years, hale and healthy, working as Loan Recovery Agent and earning Rs.25,000/- p.m.
Due to the SCCH-5 accidental injuries, and subsisting disability, the petitioner has lost the prospectus of good health, better employment etc.,
With regard to accident crime No.01/2023 is registered against the driver of the said car before the Kumbalagodu P.S. for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337, 338 and 304(A) of IPC.

Respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle and respondent No.2 being the insurer,
they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
Hence prays to allow the petition and grant compensation.
4. On service of notice, respondent No.1/owner has appeared before the tribunal and filed written statement.

In the written statement respondent No.1 denied occurrence of the accident, involvement of the offending vehicle, injuries sustained by the petitioner, treatment taken by him, expenses incurred towards SCCH-5 treatment.

Further submitted that, the Car bearing Reg.
No.KA-41-P-5894 was insured with respondent No.2 vide policy No.98000031210111216046 valid from 24.02.2022 to 23.02.2023, which is valid as on the date of accident.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.
5. Respondent No.2/insurer has appeared before the tribunal and filed written statement.
Respondent No.2 submitted that, there is no compliance of Sec.158(6) of M.V.Act.
Further submitted that, driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-41-P-5894 drove the same without having a valid and specific endorsement driving license, which is in contravention of the policy.
Further submitted that, that said vehicle was insured vide policy No.98000031210111216046 valid from 24.02.2022 to midnight of 23.02.2023.
Respondent No.2 denied age, occupation and income of the petitioner.

Further SCCH-5 submitted that, compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly Shashidhar.N vs Naveen.V on 31 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29024843/
2 excessive, arbitrary.

6. Based on the pleadings of the parties this court has framed the following:
::ISSUES::
1.

Whether Petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries due to the actionable negligent driving of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-41-P-5894 by its driver, in RTA took place on 01.01.2023 at about 12.30 p.m. on Bengaluru-Mysuru Road, near Basava Gangothri Ashrama, Kumbalagodu, Kengeri Hobli, Bengaluru City?

2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so what amount and from whom?
3. What order or award?

7. In order to prove the case, Petitioner himself examined as PW-1, examined Dr.Chidanand K.J.C.
SCCH-5 Orthopaedic Surgeon at Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma and Orthopaedics as PW-2,
Medical Record Officer at Basavanagudi Medical Centre as PW-3 and marked 18 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.18.

sentences.text:
On the other hand, Assistant Officer of respondent No.2 is examined as RW-1, PI,
APTS Yelahanka as RW-2 and marked documents as Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.3.
8.
Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record.
The counsel for respondent No.2 has filed written arguments.

9. My findings on the above issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 :
As per final order for the  following:
: : REASONS::
10. Issue No.1:- In order to prove the case, petitioner examined himself as PW-1, in his chief- SCCH-5 examination petitioner has reiterated the facts narrated in his petition.
Hence in order to avoid repetition of facts averments made in the evidence affidavit are not reiterated.

In order to prove road traffic accident PW-1 produced and marked copy of FIR as Ex.P.1, copy of FIR as Ex.P.2,
copy of spot mahazar along with sketch as Ex.P.3, copy of notice issued to owner of the vehicle and reply issued by him as Ex.P.4, copy of IMV Report as Ex.P.5, copy of charge sheet as Ex.P.7.
11.
Further to substantiate the petitioner's case, petitioner has examined Doctor as PW-2 and Medical Record Officer as PW-3.

On perusal of evidence of PW-1 to PW-3 and documents those have marked as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.7 corroborates the case of the petitioner about occurrence of the road Shashidhar.N vs Naveen.V on 31 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29024843/
3 traffic accident dated 01.01.2023 as alleged in the petition.
SCCH-5 12.
Per contra, Assistant Officer of respondent No.2 is examined as RW-1 and got marked authorization letter as Ex.R.1 and copy of insurance policy as Ex.R.2.
R.W-1 stated that the driver of car bearing Reg.No. KA- 41-P-5894 drove the same along with the four other passengers/inmates by consuming alcohol.
It is the contention of respondent No.2 that deceased Prasad hired the car for the celebration of new year and other passengers are un-authorized passengers.
As the driver of car lost his control over the vehicle and dashed to center median,to center flyover pillar and to left side wall.
As the car driver drove the car under the influence of alcohol the respondent No.2 is not liable to pay compensation as there is violation of policy condition.
13. Further examined Police Inspector, APTS, Yelahanka as RW-2 and marked copy of charge sheet as SCCH-5 Ex.R.3.
During the cross examination of R.W-2 it is elicited that as accused fled away from the spot the medical examination regarding consumption of alcohol is not done.
As per R.W-2 he collected CCTV footage regarding consumption of alcohol by the accused but said evidence is not produced before this court.
As per version of R.W-2 except filing chargesheet regarding drunken driving no cogent evidence is produced by the respondent No.2.
Thus negligence cannot be attributed to respondent No.1.

In the absence of rebuttal evidence, this tribunal held that the petitioner sustained the injuries due to the accident occurred on 01.01.2023 at about 12.30 p.m.
when he was traveling in a Car bearing Reg. No.KA-41-P-5894 on Bengaluru-Mysuru Road, near Basava Gayathri Ashrama, Kumbalagodu, Kengeri Hobli, Bengaluru.
SCCH-5 14.
It is evident from police papers that, very accident is occurred due to negligence of driver of the car bearing Reg.No.KA-41-P-5894.
Under such circumstances, considering the said evidence this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, petitioner has proved the issue No.1 in his favour.
Accordingly Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.

15. Issue No.2:- As per the evidence of the petitioner, he had sustained fracture of left femur,
fracture left 2, 3, 4, 5 ribs, fracture of left scapula, fracture of right 9, 10, 11, 12 ribs, fracture L3 and L4 vertebra, fracture of D 12 vertebra, bilateral pleural effusion with collapse of lung, spleenic injury, contusion of left kidney, fracture frontal bone, frontal sinus and ethemoid bone, fracture of sqamous bone, erector spine, scapula muscles trapezius muscles, rotator cuff muscles, SCCH-5 left deltoid muscles, left pectoralis muscles shows contusion with intramuscular emphysema and surgical emphysema, right hemothorax and left hemorhorax and other injuries, for which he underwent surgery in the form of CRIF with IMIL nailing and other supportive treatment.

In this regard he has furnished copy of wound certificate marked as Ex.P.6, discharge summary marked as Ex.P.8 issued by Basavanagudi Medical Centre, wherein he took treatment as indoor patient from 01.01.2023 to 18.01.2023 and he also took treatment as Apurva Mother and Child Hospital from 12.06.2023 to 16.06.2023.

Further he has exhibited medical bills as Ex.P.11, medical prescriptions as Ex.P.12 and X-ray Films as Ex.P.13.

sentences.text: Further Dr.Chidanand K.J.C. Orthopaedic Surgeon at Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma and SCCH-5 Orthopaedics is examined as PW-2.

To substantiate his evidence, he has exhibited OPD Record with clinical notes as Ex.P.14 and X-ray Films as Ex.P.15 and he has assessed permanent physical disability of thoraco lumbar spine injuries compression of less than 50% involving one vertebral body with no neurological manifestation at 10%.
In cross-examination he has categorically admitted that, he has not treated the petitioner and both fractures are united but in spine there is degeneration.
Further deposed that, petitioner has to undergo for surgery for removal of implant and cost of future surgery may be varied from hospital to hospital.

Under such circumstances,
considering the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner the functional disability of the petitioner is considered at the rate of 15% for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.
SCCH-5 17

. As per the case of the petitioner, he was aged about 30 years, for proof of his age, he has produced copy of aadhar card marked as Ex.P.10, wherein it is clearly mentioned date of birth of the petitioner as 30.07.1992 and the alleged accident is occurred on 01.01.2023, accordingly relying on Ex.P.10 his age is considered about 30 years as on the date of accident, hence multiplier 17 is applicable as per decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Varma and Others V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and others.

sentences.text: 18. As per his case, he was working as Loan Recovery Agent, thereby earning Rs.25,000/- p.m.
To prove the said fact, there are no documents on record.

Under such circumstances, with reference to the year of accident, relying upon the guidelines issued by Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru, SCCH-5 notional income of the petitioner is taken at the rate of Rs.16,000/-
p.m. so that, said fact is taken into consideration for the purpose of calculation of loss income during laid up period and also for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: It is admitted fact that, as per the discharge summary marked as Ex.P.8, petitioner took treatment as inpatient for 21 days.

As per the evidence of PW-2 he examined petitioner on 22.02.2024 i.e., nearly after 1 year 1 month and as per version of PW-2 and by considering the gravity of injury sustained by petitioner it may take at least three months to heal the wound.
For the said period he is entitled for the loss of income.
As SCCH-5 per the guidelines issued by Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru, notional income of the petitioner should be taken into consideration i.e., Rs.16,000/- p.m.

entities.text: Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Accordingly petitioner is entitled for the income of said quantum for the period he was admitted as inpatient in the hospital.
So petitioner is entitled for Rs.48,000/- towards loss on income during laid up period.
20. Further admittedly petitioner has exhibited Ex.P.11 medical bills for Rs.8,07,536/-.
On perusal of the said bills, it is clearly stated about spending of amount for this treatment is concerned.

Further on perusal of Ex.P.6 in which Doctor who have treated has categorically stated that,

sentences.text:
So as per Ex.P.6 wound certificate, SCCH-5 petitioner has sustained ribs fracture, scapula fracture, splenic injury,
frontal bone fracture which are grievous in nature.
Further the Investigation Officer has also filed charge sheet against Naveen V. for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 304(A), 338 of IPC.The

said charge sheet materials and evidence of PW-1 to PW-3 clearly states that, petitioner is suffering from grievous injury out of the accident caused in the alleged accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.
21.
Accordingly, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below:-

Sl.No. Head of Compensation Amount in Rs.
1.
Loss of Future Income 4,89,600-00 2. Pain and sufferings 25,000-00 3. Conveyance, nourishment and 15,000-00 attendant charges 4.
Medical Expenses 8,07,536-00 SCCH-5 5. Loss of amenities in life 15,000-00 6. Loss of income during laid up 48,000-00 period

Accordingly this tribunal hold that, the Petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.14,00,136/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization of entire amount.
23. The respondent No.2 contended that the driver of car was under the influence of alcohol at the time of accident hence respondent No.2 is not liable to pay compensation.

In this regard counsel for Respondent No.2 relied on decision reported in IFFCO TOKIO GENERAL INSURANCE LTD v/s PEARL BEVERAGES LTD wherein Hon'ble Apex court set aside the orders of NCDRC and absolved liability of insurance company by SCCH-5 holding that the driver of car was under the influence of alcohol.

entities.text: IFFCO TOKIO GENERAL INSURANCE LTD v/s PEARL BEVERAGES LTD
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the cited decision there was a claim by the owner of car damages due accident but in the case on hand due road traffic accident inmates of the car died and sustained injuries.
The respondent No.2 in the case on hand not proved through the evidence of R.W-2 that the driver of car was under the influence of alcohol.

In the case on hand, respondent No.2 being the insurer has issued insurance policy bearing No.9800003121011 1216046 which is valid for the period from 24.02.2022 to 23.02.2023, the alleged accident was occurred on 01.01.2023 it reveals that, as on the date of accident, insurance policy was in force.

Therefore the liability of respondent No.1 shall go against respondent No.2 and the respondent No.2/insurer is directed to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within SCCH-5 60 days from the date of this order.
Accordingly Issue No.2 is answered partly in the affirmative.

For the reasons assigned to Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
: :ORDER::
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.14,00,136 (Rupees fourteen lakhs one hundred and thirty six Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.2 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.

The Petitioner is entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through e-payment directly to her account on furnishing the Bank A/c details along with address proof and remaining 40% shall SCCH-5 be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in her name.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
